model.architecture: Falcon-H1 is TII's fully-hybrid design: every one of the 24 layers runs a grouped-query attention branch and a Mamba2 selective-scan branch in parallel on the same input and sums them.

variants.quantization: int8 dynamic on linears + embedding (convs and the scan stay float); fp32 activations declared for GPU

recommended.reason: measured on one Galaxy S26 with one binary: GPU 20.81 tok/s decode / 208.8 prefill, peak 2398 MB, init 12.6 s (S4 GPU gate 2026-08-24, 1 run) against CPU 19.47-20.71 decode / 160.2-202.7 prefill, peak 2696 MB, init 2.9 s (S7 Android backfill 2026-09-05, 2 cold runs). Same-device CPU control taken: decode is a wash (within 10%); gpu is kept for its prefill advantage (time to first token), a deliberate choice rather than a decode win

platform_notes: GPU execution is verified on macOS (Metal), iPhone 17 Pro (Metal), Pixel 8a (Arm Mali, OpenCL) and Qualcomm Adreno (Galaxy S26).
On low-end Android the GPU buys prefill and time-to-first-token, not decode (decode is memory-bandwidth-bound; CPU reads int8 weights, the fp32-activation GPU path reads expanded ones).
GPU runs with fp32 activations (declared in the bundle) — expect a corresponding memory multiple over CPU.
Multi-length prefill signatures (1–1024) are exported so the runtime picks tight chunks; the bundle carries the tokenizer and the stock ChatML-style Falcon-H1 chat template.
Usage example runs the GPU backend with `--backend gpu --cache no`.

Not a measured row: card reports iPhone 17 Pro gpu prefill_tps 186.8, decode_tps 25.8, ttft_s 0.88 (Performance — On device table (iPhone 17 Pro, cold start, single runs); runtime/run count not stated)

S7 Android backfill: same-device CPU control - identical binary, prompt file and flags, only --backend differs; 205-token prompt with --benchmark, 2 cold runs (compile/weight caches deleted between runs, device cooled below 42 C before each run); the GPU path does not run for this file on this handset, so this row has no GPU counterpart

known_issues: 8-question sanity gate: CPU 7/8, GPU 6/8. The shared miss ("17+25" answered "32") is reproduced verbatim by the HF bf16 reference; the GPU-only miss (8×7) is a borderline int8 greedy flip; nothing degenerates.
Arithmetic at this scale is fragile in the base model itself; int8 adds borderline greedy flips on exactly those items.
